summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an educational website created by Team Yakamoz to explore the history of human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars.

Our project presents an interactive archive where users can discover forgotten space equipment, scientific instruments, spacecraft components and other objects from NASA missions. By choosing a destination, visitors can explore individual objects, learn about their original purpose, discover the missions they belonged to and understand why they were left behind.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning lesser-known traces of space exploration into accessible and engaging historical stories. It helps preserve the history of space missions, raises awareness of their scientific achievements and encourages curiosity about space exploration.

We believe that every object left in space has a story worth telling, and future generations deserve to know it.
details:
Forgotten in Space is a website that works like a small interactive museum about objects left behind on the Moon and Mars.

We wanted to show that space missions leave behind more than just discoveries and achievements. There are also machines, rovers and different pieces of equipment that once had an important purpose but are now still sitting on the surface of another world.

On our website, users can choose between the Moon and Mars, explore different objects and learn more about them. Each object has its own photo, location and story explaining what it was used for, what happened to it and why it was left behind. We also added 3D visualizations to make exploring the planets more interesting.

We hope this project will help people learn more about space exploration in a different way. Many people know about famous missions like Apollo or the Mars rovers, but don’t always think about what happened to the equipment after those missions ended. We wanted to bring attention to these objects and the stories behind them.

We created the website using HTML, CSS and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code. We also used Three.js for the 3D planetary visualizations and NASA materials to research the objects and find reliable information and photographs.

The creative part of our project is the idea of turning forgotten space equipment into a museum. Instead of just listing facts about different missions, we wanted users to explore the objects themselves and discover their stories.

While working on the project, we focused on making the website easy to use, keeping the information understandable and accurate, choosing interesting objects, and making the visual experience fit the topic.
